We similarly read, He will violently roll (tzanof) and toss thee Like a ball (yitznofkha tzenefah) (Is. 22:18); Yea, He will wind thee round and round (ve-otekha ato) (Is. 22:17). The one who knows how the mitre is wrapped knows the meaning of [The mitre shall be removed…] this shall be no more the same: that which is low shall be exalted, and that which is high abased (Yechezkel 21:31). It takes a special skill to wind a mitre around the head. Now Scripture states, And thou shalt set the mitre upon his head, and put the holy crown upon the mitre (Shemot 29:6). The tzitz (plate) (v. 36) is thus called a nezer (crown). But upon himself shall his crown (nizro) shine (yatzitz) is similar (Tehillim 132:18). Perhaps they all are used in the sense of tzitz, meaning something seen. The same is true with the word metzitz (peereth) in He peereth through the lattice (Cant. 2:9). Note that the five senses come together in the two cavities which are in that part of the brain which is behind the forehead. This is where the imaginative power is located. Furthermore, all thoughts begin there. It is for this reason that Scripture writes, regarding the plate, that Aharon shall bear the iniquity committed in the holy things (v. 38). It is possible that those who hallowed holy things unto Hashem did so while thinking improper thoughts.

And thou shalt weave the tunic in chequer work. When Scripture first mentions Aharon’s tunic it says, a tunic of chequer work (v. 4). Only Aharon’s tunic was chequered. His sons’ tunics were not. The tunic was chequered to dignify Aharon. Scripture similar reads, And he put upon him the tunic (Vayikra 8:7) when it describes Aharon’s investiture. It reads, the tunic, the reference being to the chequered tunic. However, concerning Aharon’s children we read, and clothed them with tunics (Vayikra 8:13). The latter is similar to And for Aharon’s sons thou shalt make tunics (v. 40). Rabbi Saadiah Gaon translated ve-shibatzta (and thou shalt weave…in chequer work) as: you shall weave eye-like [designs]. It is a coin-like design, that is, a square within a circle.

And thou shalt put them upon Aharon thy brother. The word otam (them) takes in the chequered tunic, the mitre, and the girdle which are Aharon’s garments. It also takes in the unchequered tunics, the girdles, and the head-tires which are the garments of Aharon’s sons.
And consecrate them. By word of mouth. It is similar to the priest shall make him unclean (Vayikra 13:44).
Linen breeches. The linen breeches were short so that the priest would not trip over them.
When they go in. To offer incense or to kindle the lamps.
And this is the thing that thou shalt do unto them. To Aharon and his sons.

[Take.] There is no difference between lekach (take) and kach (take). We find the same to be true of tzak (pour out) and yetzak (pour) in Pour out (tzak) for the people, that they may eat (Melachim II 4:41) and in And also pour (yetzak) water into it (Yechezkel 24:3).

[One young bullock.] The fact that Scripture notes that the par (bull) was a ben bakar (of the herd) indicates that the par (bull) was young. The same applies to the phrase bene yonah (turtle-doves) (Vayikra 1:14), and the phrase se’_ir izzim (a goat) (Vayikra 4:23).
[And two rams.] An ayal (ram) is older than a keves (lamb). The fact that the drink offering for an ayal (ram) consists of a third of a hin and that of a keves (lamb) a quarter of a hin proves this.
And unleavened…cakes. They were thick, as wafers unleavened proves.

[With oil.] Scripture reads ba-shemen (with oil). The reference, in keeping with the rule, is to olive oil. [Of FINE WHEATEN FLOUR.] The word solet (fine flour) refers to flour made from wheat cleansed of all impurities. It is called samid in Arabic. It is produced in the land of the Yishmeelim. There is no better bread than bread made from it. Many connect the word solet to the word salita (thou hast trodden) in Thou hast trodden light all them that err from Thy statutes (Tehillim 119:118); and to sillah (trodden) in Hashem hath trodden All my mighty men in the midst of me (Eichah 1:15). They say that makkolet (food) in food to your household (Melachim I 5:25) is similar. Others say that solet means ground.
And bring them in the basket. You shall bring the bread, which is in the basket as the law requires, to the door of the tent of meeting. The same applies to the bullock and the rams.
And thou shalt take the garments. The breastplate (choshen) is called a garment because it covers that part of the body which lies opposite the heart.

And thou shalt set. It is also not beyond the realm of possibility that Moshe placed the mitre on Aharon last. Scripture mentions the mitre before the girdle at the opening of the Torah portion because the mitre is more important than the girdle.

His head. Only on Aharon’s head, as he was the anointed priest. Now Aharon was anointed before the mitre was placed on his head, for Moshe poured the oil only upon the head. We similarly read, It is like the precious oil upon the head, Coming down upon the beard; Even Aharon’s beard (Tehillim 133:2).
And thou shalt bring his sons. To the door of the tent of meeting.

And thou shalt gird them with girdles. Girdles takes in Aharon’s girdle and the girdle of his sons. Similarly the breeches. After stating them, Scripture goes on to explain that the reference is to Aharon and his sons. It is similar to And she opened it, and saw it, even the child (Shemot 2:6).
[And bind.] The word ve-chavashta (and bind) is similar to the word chovesh (healer) in I will not be a healer (Is. 3:7).

And thou shalt consecrate. The one who translated the Torah into Aramaic is of the opinion that u-milleta yad (and thou shalt consecrate) is similar to u-milu yadav (so shall they consecrate it) (Yechezkel 43:26). However, what shall we do with milu yedkhem ha-yom (consecrate yourselves today to the Lord) (Shemot 32:29)? Saadiah Gaon explains the word yad to mean obligation. Others say that the term melu’im (consecration) is used because it indicates that they are complete, full, and trained. However, what will they do with u-mile’u yadav (so shall they consecrate it) (Yechezkel 43:26)?

And thou shalt bring the bullock. This has already been mentioned. Its meaning is as follows. When you shall bring the bullock, Aharon and his sons shall lay their hands upon it. Some say that the meaning of and Aharon shall lay is: Aharon alone shall first lay his hands upon the head of the bullock. His sons shall then do the same. Now with regard to the ram, Scripture later states, and Aharon and his sons shall lay their hands upon the head of the ram (v. 15). Scripture thus describes exactly what happened. They should lay their hands together, not one after the other.
And thou shalt kill the bullock. Moshe slaughtered the bullock.

[Before Hashem.] Scripture reads, before Hashem, because the ark was in the center of the western side of the tabernacle. The incense altar was directly aligned with it. So was the altar of the burnt offerings.
He shall pour out. The priest who pours shall pour out.
And thou shalt take. Bullock and goats do not have a fat tail (alyah).

[Kidneys.] Some say that kelayot (kidneys) are so called because the word kelayot is related to the word kaletah (pineth) in My soul yearneth, yea even pineth for the courts of the Lord (Tehillim 84:3). For the power of sexual desire is located in the kidneys.
But the flesh of the bullock. Flesh takes in the head and the pieces of the bullock.
And its dung. Logically speaking, it was to be washed and then it was to be burned.. AND HE SHALL MAKE THEM SMOKE (ve-hiktir). The reference is to the enumerated organs.

[Sin-offering.] A sin offering is called a chatat because it is brought to atone for a sin. The same applies to the asham (guilt-offering). Hence the meaning of ve-chitte’u et ha-mizbe’ach (they shall purify the altar) is: they shall remove the sin from the altar.
Thou shalt also take the one ram. Any one of the two rams which you decide to choose.

And thou shalt slay the ram, and thou shalt take its blood and dash it round about against the altar. Not on the corners of the altar. Look, he [Moshe] shall dash all the blood round about against the altar and not upon the base of the altar.
And the ram. Scripture does not mention that Moshe was commanded to cut the bullock into pieces. It was therefore entirely burned. Hence Scripture does not mention the bullock’s legs.
And wash. By command.
And thou shalt make the whole ram smoke. Hence the fat tail and the fat are not mentioned.
And thou shalt take. This second ram served as the ram of consecration.
Then thou shalt kill…tip. The word tenukh (tip) has no counterpart. Saadiah Gaon says that it refers to the soft tissue which is connected to the circle of the ear.
The great toe. The plural of bohen (great toe) is behonot (Jud. 1:6). This is grammatically inconsistent. This noun is thus vocalized according to two paradigms. There are many such nouns.
[And dash the blood.] The blood of the second ram shall be dashed like the blood of the first ram. The reference is only to the remaining blood.
And thou shalt take of the blood that is upon the altar…and sprinkle it upon Aharon, and upon his garments. Beneath his garments and upon his garments.
And thou shalt take of the ram the fat. The reference is to the fat that is upon the innards, as stated in the Torah portion Va-Yikra.

The right thigh. The thigh that is on the right side and the breast were taken from the ram of consecration. From that day on, the thigh and the breast of peace offerings were to be given to Aharon and his sons. However, Moshe alone ate the breast of the ram of consecration because he was a high priest.
And one loaf of bread. The reference is to the unleavened bread (v. 2).
And shalt wave them. While they are in the hands of Aharon and his sons.
And thou shalt take them from their hands. Our verse states, from their hands. Elsewhere Scripture states, from off their hands (Vayikra 8:28). They mean the same thing.
A sweet savour. The chet is doubled in nicho’ach (sweet savour). [A SWEET SAVOUR BEFORE THE Hashem.] The one who understands the secret of man’s soul will understand this.
An offering. The word issheh (offering) is an adjective. It is related to the word esh (fire). Scripture elsewhere states, from the fire (Bamidbar 18:9).
And thou shalt take. From Aharon’s ram. Aharon’s sons are not mentioned, as Aharon was the principal.
[Portion.] The word manah means a portion.

And thou shalt sanctify. From this day and henceforth. Waving and heaving are not identical. For what is heaved is lifted up. It is not waved. The meaning of even their heave-offering (v. 28) is: the heave offerings which they will separate from peace offerings, shall be heaved in honor of Hashem.
And the holy garments of Aharon shall be for his sons after him. Shall be for his son who is anointed in his place.
[After him.] After his death.

Seven days. The word yilbasham (put them on) is vocalized with a long rather than a short kamatz. The word amilam (I will cut them off) in Verily, in the name of Hashem I will cut them off (Tehillim 118:10) is similar.
And seethe. By command. It is similar to and thou shalt smite the rock (Shemot 17:6), and to So Shlomo built the house (Melachim I 6:14).
And Aharon and his sons shall eat. The bread remaining in the basket.
And they shall eat those things. The verse is abridged.
[Them.] The word otam (them) also refers to something else.
But a stranger. Who is not of Aharon’s seed.
And if aught. The ram of consecration is so called because they are consecrated by it.

Thee. The word otakhah has an etnach beneath it. Otakhah is a combination of otakh (thee) (Bereshit 39:9), which is vocalized with a long kamatz beneath the tav, and otekha (thee) in for thee have I seen (Bereshit 7:1).
And every day shalt thou offer the bullock. Every day of the seven days of consecration.

[Beside the other offerings of atonement.] Its meaning is, in addition to the two rams. Scripture further states, As hath been done this day, so Hashem hath commanded to do, to make atonement for you (Vayikra 8:34).
Most holy. The meaning of kodesh kodashim (most holy) is holy like any other holy object.

Whatsoever touches the altar shall be holy. This is similar to Whatsoever shall touch the flesh thereof shall be holy (Vayikra 6:20). Some say that the verse speaks only of the bread. Scripture is telling us that if the bread is not holy, that is, if the bread is unclean, then it shall not touch the altar.

Now this is. Its meaning is: now this is the sacrifice. Similarly, the meaning of This they shall give (Shemot 30:13) is: this amount they shall give. Similarly And this is that thou shalt make it (Bereshit 6:15). Moshe shall do this during the seven days of consecration. Afterwards Aharon and his sons shall do likewise.

The one lamb. The heh prefixed to the word keves (lamb) also serves as a prefix to the word echad (one). The phrase is to be read as if written, et ha-keves ha-echad (the one lamb). Rabbi Moshe Ha-Kohen says that the meaning of et ha-keves echad is, the lamb, one lamb.
A tenth part. A tenth part of an ephah.
[A hin.] Also note that hin is a Mitzri measure.
And. The word u-kheniskah (and according to the drink offering thereof) refers to boker (morning).

It shall be a continual burnt-offering throughout your generations. They shall bring these offerings when they enter the land of Kenaan. For Bnei Yisrael offered burnt offerings only for fifty days in the desert of Sinai. This is what Scripture means by It is a continual burnt-offering, which was offered in mount Sinai (Bamidbar 28:6). The tabernacle was placed at the edge of the camp at the bottom of the mount, as the tribes were intermingled. On the first day of the second month they began to know the number of each tribe and to make standards (Bamidbar 1 and 2). After they traveled a distance of a three-day journey from Mount Sinai, the ark journeyed in the midst of the camps (Bamidbar 10:33). Logically speaking, Bnei Yisrael offered burnt offerings and sacrifices only at Sinai and on Yom Kippur in the second year. This is what Scripture states regarding Aharon’s service. The Torah there writes, And he [Aharon] did as Hashem commanded Moshe (Vayikra 16:34). Scripture similarly states, Did ye bring unto Me sacrifices and offerings in the wilderness forty years, O house of Yisrael? (Amos 5:25). Yisrael spent about thirty-eight years in a wasteland, in a howling wilderness (Devarim 32:10). Where did they get half a hin of olive oil and a half hin of wine daily? How could they carry almost fourteen thousand hin around with them? Where did they get two lambs daily in the first year? Where did they get the animals for the additional sacrifices on the Sabbath and the festivals? The statement we and our cattle (Bamidbar 20:4) does not refute our contention, for Yisrael was then at Kadesh, and they bought cattle from the settled population. Furthermore, they looted the Midyanim and the lands of Sichon and Og in that year. They thus had an abundance of cattle.
[I will meet.] Scripture clearly explains the reason that the tabernacle is called the ohel mo’ed (the tent of meeting).
With you. Yisrael. We find this to be the case when the congregation was called together.

To speak there unto thee. To speak there alone to you. However, Yefet says that the meaning of I will meet with you is: with Moshe and occasionally with Aharon. He maintains that to speak there unto thee hints that God will continually speak there with Moshe. He offers, And there I will meet with the children of Yisrael (v. 43) as proof.

And [the tent] shall be sanctified by my glory. I believe that the tent of meeting was the place of meeting because it took in everything, namely, the tabernacle and all its utensils, the ark, and the three objects. The tent will be sanctified by My glory, which will rest on the cherubim.

And I will sanctify the Tent of Meeting. It is because of the glory that the tent is holy, for it was sanctified by the glory. The altar that stood before the opening of the tent of meeting was similarly sanctified.
Aharon also and his sons will I sanctify. I will sanctify Aharon and his sons, who minister in the tent of meeting and upon the altar.

And I will dwell. Scripture describes how God’s glory will dwell among the children of Yisrael when the standards will be set up. Four standards were set up on the four sides. Additionally, there was a separation between the camp of the Leviyim and the camp of Bnei Yisrael because they too camped on all four sides, There was another barrier beyond this barrier where the tent of meeting was placed amidst the children of Yisrael. Now a person who experienced a seminal emission did not have to leave the camp of Yisrael. Neither was there a place set aside beyond the border of the camp for a person to sit down [and relieve himself]. The commandment for a person who experienced a seminal emission to leave the camp applied only to the camp of Yisrael when it went to war against the enemy. The commandment When thou goest forth in camp against thine enemies (Devarim 23:10) similarly does not speak of the entire camp of Yisrael, men, women, and children. It is only males, and then only a small number of them, who sally out to wage war. Now when the soldiers of Yisrael carried the ark with them as Phineas did, they were unable to set up a barrier between themselves and the place of the ark.

And they shall know. Its meaning is, then they shall know that the only reason that I took them out of Mitzrayim was so that they would make a sanctuary for Me that I may dwell among them. This is what Scripture means by ye shall serve Elokim upon this mountain (Shemot 3:12).

And thou shalt make an altar to burn incense upon. The word miktar (to burn) is an infinitive. It is like the word u-mishlo’ach (and of sending) in and of sending portions one to another (Esther 9:19).
A cubit. The altar was a half a cubit higher than the table. Perhaps it was similarly half a cubit higher than the menorah. The altar was aligned with the cherubim which spread their wings upward.

And thou shalt overlay it with pure gold. A top is mentioned with regard to the altar of incense. Scripture does not mention a top with regard to the brass altar. The altar was called the golden altar because it was overlaid with gold. The same applies to The pure table (Vayikra 24:6). It is like the pure candlestick (Vayikra 24:4).
Upon the two sides of it. Scripture states this in order to be especially clear.
[Wherewith.] THE heh at the end of the word ba-hemmah (wherewith) is superfluous, as I have already noted, since hemmah is penultimately accented.
And thou shalt make the staves of acaciawood. And overlay them with gold like the staves of the ark.
And thou shalt put it before the veil. On the outside.
Before the ark-cover. The altar should be aligned with the ark cover.

And Aharon shall burn thereon incense of sweet spices. Along with other spices (besamim). It is possible that the sammim (sweet spices) were the most important ingredient. It is also possible that Scripture mentions sammim (spices) in order to distinguish between the compounds, as one of the compounds consisted only of besamim (spices). It did not contain sammim (sweet spices).
[When he dresseth.] When he fixes the wick and the oil.
Lighteth the lamps. Scripture employs be-he’alot for lighting because the flame of the wick goes up. Be-he’alot is clearly a transitive verb.
A perpetual incense. When they offer burnt offerings. Scripture therefore says, throughout your generations.
Ye shall offer no strange incense. An incense which is not its exact duplicate.
And Aharon shall make atonement upon the horns of it once in the year. On the tenth day of the seventh month.

[Of atonement.] The reference is to the blood of the bullock and the blood of the he-goat. The aforementioned is a yearly obligation. There is no reason for Scripture to mention the blood of the bullock brought by the anointed high priest when he sins and the blood of the bullock brought by the congregation when they sin. For they are not placed on the horns of the altar at fixed times. They are placed there only on rare occasions.
May the name of the exalted God be eternally blessed. He did every good for Yisrael.
To His messenger He revealed every secret In the Torah portion called Ki Tissa.

[When thou takest the sum.] Scripture begins to explain the law of the atonement money which each and every one is obligated to give. The atonement money was not a free will offering. Scripture makes mention of the atonement money here because it notes above that atonement shall be made [upon the horns of the altar of incense] once a year. The atonement money was, as I will explain, similarly to be given once a year. The description of the laver and its base follow next because they are not to be made from free will gifts of the congregation but only from the mirrors of the women who performed tasks. Scripture also mentions the anointing oil and the sweet incense, for the princes alone brought them. Now since Scripture mentions the anointing oil it mentions the vessels which were anointed. Scripture also mentions the great craftsman, the perfumer, and the one whose counsel guided those who constructed the entire tabernacle, namely, Betzalel and Oholiav [who was with him]. Scripture mentions the Sabbath in order to warn Bnei Yisrael at the beginning not to do Hashem’s work on the Sabbath. Scripture next records the prayer offered by Moshe before he came down from the mountain. However, it first had to mention the making of the golden calf so that we would know why Moshe prayed. Scripture then tells of Moshe’s descent from the mountain, the burning of the calf, and Moshe’s return to the mountain to pray for Yisrael a second time. Scripture mentions that Moshe’s anger caused him to move his tent outside the camp of Yisrael. However, some say that Scripture records what happened. Scripture then mentions Moshe’s great glory, namely, that Moshe saw Hashem’s glory. It tells us that Hashem then commanded Moshe to descend and hew out tablets. It informs us that Hashem inscribed the tablets a second time. Scripture mentions the conditions upon which Hashem made a treaty with Yisrael. These conditions are recorded in the Torah portion Ve-Ellaeh Ha-Mishpatim. Scripture then mentions that the skin of Moshe’s face shone when Moshe came down from the mountain with the tablets of the covenant in his hand. Rabbi Saadiah Gaon says that the atonement money was an annual obligation upon Yisrael. It was obligatory whether their king counted them or not. Saadiah Gaon offers the census taken by Moshe in the desert as proof. Saadiah says that the money collected was used for the congregational sacrifices, the construction of the laver, the making of the anointing oil, and the sweet incense. Part of it was also given to the Sanhedrin. Betzalel and Oholiav allude to this. [WHEN THOU TAKEST THE SUM.] It is customary for the accountants who are intimate with the details of an account to itemize upon pages. However they write the sum of all the items at the head of the page. Some say that the plague which occurred in the days of David struck because Yisrael did not offer a ransom for their soul. If this is true it refutes the opinion of Saadiah Gaon.

[When thou numberest them.] The meaning of that there be no plague among them, when thou numberest them is: if they do not give atonement money at the very moment of the numbering, a plague will strike. However, Yefet says it means that if they are numbered and do not give their ransom, they will fall before their enemies when they go to war.
This. This amount. It is similar to And this thou shalt make it (Bereshit 7:15).

[Every one that passeth.] The meaning of every one that passeth is everyone who passes his twentieth year. Twenty years is about three weeks of years [almost twenty-one years]. A person’s mind is then fully developed. His body also no longer grows in height.
[Gerahs.] These gerahs refer to the pits of a carob.
Every one…that are numbered. Pekudim (that are numbered) is active.
The rich. Scripture explains why the rich shall not give more, and the poor shall not give less. The reason for this is that the money is an atonement for one’s soul.
And thou shalt take…and shalt appoint it for the service of the Tent of Meeting. This is explained in the Torah portion Ve-Ellah Pekude.
[That it may be a memorial for the children of Yisrael.] For the tabernacle stood only upon sockets which were made from the atonement money as a memorial for the children of Yisrael.
And the Lord spoke. A new section begins here.

And the base thereof. Kanno means the base thereof. The bases that Shlomo made proves this. Now Scripture states that the laver was placed between the tent of meeting and the altar. This shows that the altar was not adjacent to the door of the tent but was close to it The altar was placed in the center and was aligned with the altar of incense. The laver was placed between the tent and the altar, towards one of the sides. However, Scripture does not mention this. It does not seem logical for the laver to be aligned with the altar of incense and thus be aligned with the ark cover.

Shall wash. Scripture mentions that the laver was necessary because of those who served in the tabernacle, namely, Aharon and his sons and their descendants. Moshe is not now mentioned, as Moshe alone used the laver as long as he lived. However, Scripture mentions Moshe’s use of the laver when it describes the actual setting up of the laver.

When they go into the Tent of Meeting, they shall wash with water. The meaning of yirchatzu mayim is they shall wash with water. The reason the hands and feet have to be washed is that they are the active parts of the body. There are many such instances.

ורחצו (And they shall wash) - He reiterated and mentioned it another time [he had already written so in verse 19], to instruct that they should do so always [for future generations]. Or, he mentioned this [to add a punishment to the warning, to indicate] that if they do not do so, they are liable to death [as it is stated 'and they shall not die'; and so Rashi explains].
Moreover the Lord spoke. This is a section unto itself.

Take thou also unto thee. Kach lekha (take unto thee) is similar to lekh leha (get thee out) (Bereshit 12:1) and u-kechu lakhem tzon (and take you lambs) (Shemot 12:21). According to the plain meaning of the text, aseh lekha saraf (make thee a fiery serpent) (Bamidbar 21:8) and also pesal lekha (hew thee) (Shemot 34:1) are similar, for such is the way of the Hebrew language.

[Myrrh.] The word mor (myrrh) is difficult. Saadiah Gaon translated it as musk. It thus does not come from trees even though it has a pleasant odor. Perhaps this is the reason Scripture separates it from the spices. For Scripture states, I have gathered my myrrh with my spice (Cant. 5:1). Myrrh is thus gathered. Those who provide musk say that it is produced in the throat of a deer. Behold, Scripture states, And my hands dropped with myrrh (Cant. 5:5). Perhaps this is the case when the myrrh is wet.

[The chief spices.] Scripture reads besamim rosh (the chief spices) to indicate that the top of each spice is to be taken. The top of the spice is of a much better quality than that which remains at the end. [AND OF SWEET CINNAMON.] Having said kinnemon (cinnamon), what reason is there for Scripture to add besem (sweet)? It is possible that Scripture reads, ve-kinnemon besem, because the cinnamon had to be of the best quality. The same also applies to the calamus. [HALF SO MUCH, EVEN TWO HUNDRED AND FIFTY.] The ancients, of blessed memory, said that all the ingredients were of equal weight. We will accept what they say. However, we do not know why Scripture says, half so much even two hundred and fifty. I do not understand the reason for the halves for it is the practice in all of the lands of the Yishmeelim not to add even the weight of a mustard seed to anything being weighed. They most certainly do not add anything to any ingredient used in the work of a perfumer.
Cassia. We know from tradition that kiddah is cassia.
And thou shalt make it…a perfume compounded after the art of the perfumer. Rokach mirkachat (a perfume compounded after the art of the perfumer) is similar to miktar ketoret (to burn incense) (v. 1).
[It shall be a holy anointing oil.] This is what Scripture refers to next.
And thou shalt anoint therewith the Tent of Meeting. This includes the entire tabernacle. Our verse mentions the ark. the most important object in the tent of meeting.
And the table. The table is mentioned first because it was the largest [object in the sanctuary] and it had many utensils. Scripture then mentions the menorah, which had many utensils.
And the altar of burnt-offering. It had many vessels.
And thou shalt sanctify. With the anointing oil.

[Whatsoever toucheth them shall be holy.] We can derive the meaning of whatsoever toucheth them shall be holy from If one bear hallowed flesh (Chaggai 2:12), which, according to the plain meaning of the text, is be taken literally. The verse teaches: if holy flesh touches bread, pottage, wine, oil, or any food it becomes holy. The same applies to the altar of burnt offering, as Scripture also uses the term “most holy” regarding it.
And thou shalt anoint Aharon and his sons. Alone, no one else.
This shall be a holy anointing oil. All oil made according to this composition shall be used to anoint the seed of Aharon.

Shall it not be poured. Rabbi Merinus says that yisakh (poured) has the same meaning as yusakh. Similarly, va-yisem (he was put) in and he was put in a coffin (Bereshit 50: 26) has the same meaning as va-yusam. [UPON THE FLESH OF MAN SHALL IT NOT BE POURED.] Scripture states, Upon the flesh of man shall it not be poured because it was customary in Yisrael for men and also for women to anoint themselves with oil. For Scripture states, but thou shalt not anoint thyself with oil (Devarim 28:40). It is prohibited for a priest and certainly for anyone else to anoint themselves with this oil, for the anointing oil was poured upon the head of the anointed.
According to the composition thereof. Oil composed of the exact amount of the above-listed spices.

Whosoever. The meaning of or whosoever putteth any of it on a stranger (zar) is: or whosoever putteth any of it on someone who is not of Aharon’s family. Saadiah Gaon, of blessed memory, says that Yisrael had a tradition that David and his seed should be anointed with the anointing oil. Other kings were not to be so anointed. The Gaon was compelled to explain thus because Tzadok took some of the anointing oil that was in the tent of meeting and used it to anoint Shlomo. Yefet says that on a stranger means on someone who is not a Yisraeli. However, he was mistaken, for Scripture states, and the stranger (zar) that draweth nigh shall be put to death (Bamidbar 3:10). The meaning of the latter is: To the end that no stranger (zar), that is not of the seed of Aharon, draw near (Bamidbar 17:5). Others say that this law refers only to the oil made by Moshe. However, this also does not appear to me to be correct. For Scripture first states, This shall be a holy anointing oil unto Me throughout your generations (v. 31). Furthermore, the Pentateuch states (v. 33), Whosoever, compoundeth any like it, or whosoever putteth any of “a similarly compounded oil” upon a stranger. Thus there is no difference between the anointing oil made by Moshe and its duplicate which was made later. Scripture does not state, “except for the family of David.” I believe that all the commandments are obligatory on all the generations of Yisrael. The law stating that no burnt offering should be offered in any but the chosen place is an example. Nevertheless, we find that Gidon, Shmuel, and also Eliyahu at Mount Karmel brought burnt offerings. I mentioned Gidon because he offered burnt offerings even though he was not a priest. The same is true of Shmuel. The fact that he was descended from Korach is of no avail. These acts were all based on temporary [ad hoc] rulings. We can say the same also with regard to Shlomo. Shlomo was anointed with the anointing oil on the temporary ruling of the prophet Natan or Gad.

Take unto thee sweet spices. The ancients, of blessed memory, received a tradition that there were eleven types of spices. Now the verse that notes that spices were to be used in the sweet incense does not list the spices that were to be used in the sweet incense. Scripture mentions the sweet spices. However, Scripture does not mention their weight.
[Sweet spices.] Scripture mentions sammim (sweet spices) a second time because it wants to say: take the aforementioned sweet spices, and along with them, take pure frankincense.
Of each shall there be a like weight. Each spice to be compounded by itself. It shall then be mixed.

And thou shalt make…seasoned with salt. Memullach (seasoned with salt) means seasoned with salt from Sedom. Others say that memullach means thinly ground. Or it is related to the word melechah (salt) in A salt land (Jer. 17:6).
And thou shalt beat some of it very small. As thin as you are able to make it. This is the perpetual incense which was offered on the golden altar.
And the incense which thou shalt make. This alludes to Moshe.
Ye shall not make. Yisrael is being spoken to.
It shall be unto thee holy. The priest, or all of Yisrael. Remember the days of old (Devarim 32:7) is similar.
Whosoever. Scripture first warns. It then mentions the punishment, as is the law.

And the Lord spoke. Rabbi Saadiah Gaon asked, “Why were Betzalel and Oholiav chosen?” He answered that Betzalel was chosen because he was descended from Yehudah, whom Yaakov compared to a lion’s whelp (Bereshit 49:9). Oholiav was chosen because he was descended from Dan, whom Moshe also compared to a lion’s whelp (Devarim 33:22). The lion is narrow at the end. The temple was similarly narrow at the end. Now this is a preacher’s homily, for Betzalel and Oholiav did not build the temple. The width of the tabernacle which they made did not vary. There is no basis for Saadiah Gaon’s question. Betzalel and Oholiav were chosen because there was no one in Yisrael who equaled them.
See. With a respectful eye.

[I have called by name Betzalel.] Betzalel is the one being called. The meaning of I have called by name Betzalel is: I have called Betzalel’s name because he has no equal in ability to construct the tabernacle.

[Betzalel the son of Uri, the son of Chur.] According to the plain meaning of the text, Kalev the son of Yefuneh is not to be identified with Kalev the son of Chetzron. There is indisputable evidence that this is so. Intelligent people will understand the proof.

And I have filled him. This is similar to And Yehoshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom (Devarim 34:9). [AND I HAVE FILLED HIM WITH THE SPIRIT OF GOD, IN WISDOM, AND IN UNDERSTANDING.] Scripture states, And the spirit of Hashem shall rest upon him (Is. 11:2). It then goes on to explain that the spirit of Hashem is The spirit of wisdom and understanding (Ibid.). Wisdom (chokhmah) refers to the type of intelligence that is stored in the back of the brain. The word tevunah (understanding) and also the word binah (reason) are related to the word ben (between). They refer to the intellectual faculty that lies in the middle cavity of the brain between knowledge and wisdom. For wisdom is situated in the posterior cavity of the brain, and knowledge, which is gathered by the senses, is located in the cavities of the brain that are adjacent to the forehead. Knowledge is called al takyil in Arabic. Understanding is called al fakrah and wisdom al hakhmah. Now Betzalel was endowed with every wisdom. He mastered the science of mathematics, geometry, proportions, astronomy, biology, and the secret of the human soul. He also towered over the people of his generation in that he knew all manner of workmanship. Many intelligent people do not possess even one practical skill. Hence Scripture prefixes a vav to the word kol (and) and reads, u-vekhol melakhah (and in all manner of workmanship).
With him. Equal to him in workmanship but not in the science of cutting. Observe, the meaning of and in all manner of workmanship is (v. 3) to devise skilful works (v. 4).
And in the hearts of all that are wise-hearted I have put wisdom. To do work. Also one finds in human nature the ability to devise intricate geometric forms without ever having studied this science.
[That they may make all that I have commanded.] Scripture now goes on to mention all the objects which they were required to make.
The Tent of Meeting. Scripture starts with the tent of meeting because it includes everything in the tabernacle. It mentions the ark and the ark cover because of their great importance.
And all the furniture of the tent. The curtain, the veil, the boards, and the bars. It mentions the table in accordance with what I have already noted.

And the plaited garments. The bigde ha-serad (the plaited garments) were garments used to cover the ark, the table, the altar, [and] the menorah when journeying. Scripture goes on to explain, And of the blue, and purple, and scarlet, they made plaited garments (bigde serad) (Shemot 39:1). Each is listed separately as the Torah portion Ba-Midbar Sinai (Bamidbar 4:6-14) states. Scripture then states, [And of the blue, and purple, and the scarlet] they made plaited garments…and [they] made the holy garments [for Aharon] (Shemot 39:1). It then goes on to list them. Observe! The word serad is related to the word sarid (remain) in escape or remain (Yirmiyahu 44:14).
For the holy place. They are for the need of the holy place.
Saying. Every time the word lemor (saying) is used with va-yedabber (he spoke), its meaning is, saying to him. Here its meaning is, to tell Yisrael.

Thou. Since Hashem commanded Yisrael to construct the tabernacle, Yisrael might think that they should occupy themselves with the construction of the tabernacle on the Sabbath. Hence Scripture states, Verilyye shall keep My sabbaths. One of the great sages said that it is well-known that only one Sabbath is Hashem’s Sabbath. Now, if this is so, then what is the meaning of My sabbaths? He answered that the world will exist for six thousand years. The seventh millennium and also the Sabbatical year are thus Sabbaths. However, My sabbaths refers to the many Sabbaths of the year. Note that we do not find the term shabbat used with reference to the festivals. The term used is shabbaton (a solemn rest). There is a controversy regarding the meaning of from the morrow after the sabbath (Vayikra 23:15). The traditional interpretation is correct. However, as I will explain in its place, it requires interpretation. The Day of Atonement is called Yisrael’s Sabbath, not Hashem’s Sabbath.
For it is a sign. I will explain at the end of the chapter what the Sabbath signifies.
Who sanctify you. When you sanctify the Sabbath, which I sanctified, and refrain from doing any work on the Sabbath day.

Ye shall keep the Sabbath…every one that profaneth it shall surely be put to death. Mot yumat (he shall surely be put to death) means: it is possible he will be put to death. It is similar to and its owner also shall be put to death (Shemot 21:29). The verse stating I [God] will cut off whosoever doeth any work on the Sabbath in secret or in front of a witness is proof of the above.

Six days. Scripture goes on to explain that they are permitted to do work on the other six days of the week. The word ye’aseh (shall be done) governs the word melakhah (work). Perhaps the word kol (any) or devar ma’aseh (an act of) is missing. Now its meaning is, you shall kill him if he does work in public.

Shall keep. They shall keep count of the days of the week so that they do not forget which day is the Sabbath. One shall set his affairs in order and take care of his needs on the sixth day so that he will keep the Sabbath and not desecrate it.
The meaning of la’asot (to observe) in la’asot et ha-shabbat (to observe the Sabbath) is thus similar to the meaning of la’asot (to dress) in and he hastened to dress (la’asot) it. (Bereshit 18:7).

It is a sign between me and the children of Yisrael. Scripture employs the terms covenant and sign with regard to circumcision. It does the same with regard to the Sabbath. Rabbi Saadiah Gaon says: When people find a male circumcised in such a way that the glans penis is uncovered, then they will know that he is a Yisraeli. Similarly when a person refrains from doing any work or engaging in business on the Sabbath. However, I believe that the meaning of It is a sign is, for in six days the Lord made heaven and earth. Thus the one who does work on the Sabbath denies the work of creation.

[For in six days Hashem made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day he ceased from work and rested.] The Torah employs human language so that those who hear its words will understand. Scripture’s statement, And rested, is to be taken metaphorically because Hashem…fainteth not, neither is weary (Is. 40:28). Look, the hosts of heaven, namely, the glorious corporeal entities which Hashem created, circle the sky day and night eternally. This is certainly the case with the glorious incorporeal entities. It is most certainly true of the Creator of all, Who Inhabits eternity (Is. 57:15), and is enthroned of old (Tehillim 55:20), who does all by command without any movement on His part.

And he gave. Empty heads ask, “What did Moshe do on the mount for forty days and forty nights?” They do not know that if Moshe spent this number and double its double in years with Hashem, he would barely know one part of a thousand of Hashem’s work and ways and the secret of all the precepts which Hashem commanded him. They think that deeds are most important. This is not so. What is important is heart together with deed. Heart and tongue train a person [to observe the commandments]. We thus read, in thy mouth, and in thy heart, that thou mayest do it (Devarim 30:14). Our ancients said, “Hashem desires the heart.” Loving Hashem and cleaving to Hashem with all of one’s soul is the basis of the commandments. This cannot be completely accomplished if a person does not know the ways of Hashem and is not acquainted with Hashem’s work in the upper and lower worlds. The prophet thus states, But let him that glorieth glory in this, That he understandeth and knoweth Me (Yirmiyahu 9:23). It will then become clear to a person that Hashem exercises mercy, Justice, and righteous, in the earth (Ibid.). A person cannot know Hashem if he does not know his own spirit, soul, and body. For of what use is a person’s wisdom to him if he does not know the makeup of his soul? Now Moshe, who prophesied in the desert for forty years and was party to many secrets which Hashem revealed to him on Mount Sinai, said before his death, O Hashem Hashem, Thou hast begun to show Thy servant Thy greatness (Devarim 3:24). Thus it was only then that Moshe began to understand Hashem’s greatness and that Hashem’s greatness was shown to him. This is truth, for His greatness is unsearchable (Tehillim 145:3).

Tables of stone. I have already explained this. [WITH THE FINGER OF GOD.] Scripture’s statement with the finger of Elokim is an anthropomorphism, for Hashem’s will is accomplished by the word coming out of Elokim’s mouth. Elokim’s mouth is employed metaphorically. Elokim is said to act like human kings. This is how For He commanded, and they were created (Tehillim 118:27) is to be understood. Elokim’s words appear to man to be standing in heaven. Scripture clearly states, Thy word standeth fast in heaven (Tehillim 119:89). The intelligent will understand.

Avraham the author says: I must dwell at length on the incident of the golden calf. Some of the ancients said that Chur was killed. Aharon thus was afraid. There is an opinion that Aharon feared for Yisrael, that if they killed him Elokim in return would destroy all of Yisrael. Let us now turn to the plain meaning of the text. If the making of the golden calf entailed idolatry, why was Aharon afraid that he would be killed? Did not many pious Bnei Yisrael of later generations, whose level of piety did not even reach to the bottom of the sole of Aharon’s foot, die for the sake of the unity of Elokim’s name? Look! Daniel’s companions were thrown into a fiery furnace because they refused to bow before an image. How then could Aharon make an idol, which is worse than bowing down to it? Was not Aharon one of Elokim’s holy people? Was he not a prophet to Yisrael? Many commandments were given by him and his brother Moshe. If Aharon was afraid to die then Chur was superior to him. If Aharon made an idol then Moshe was obligated to kill him before he killed those who worshipped the calf. However, Moshe prayed for Aharon and killed the worshippers. How could Aharon and his seed later on, for all eternity, make atonement for the children of Yisrael? Do not pay attention to Take thee a bull-calf for a sin-offering (Vayikra 9:2), for the bull-calf was not brought because Aharon made the golden calf. On the Day of Atonement all anointed priests are similarly commanded to bring a young bullock for a sin offering. We cannot say that the bullock was brought because of their father’s sin, because all the priests were descended from Elazar and Itamar. Pinchas was also already born by the time the golden calf was made. Furthermore, the portion dealing with the laws of the Day of Atonement commands Yisrael to bring a he-goat for a sin offering. Now Yisrael did not make an image in the form of a he-goat. The red heifer similarly was not brought to atone for idolatry. It was brought to purify the unclean. All philosophers admit that Elokim will not choose a person whom He knows will ultimately worship idols to serve as His messenger. Not every prophet is a messenger. Now Scripture tells us that shortly before Moshe died, he said, Thy Tumim and Thy Urim be with Thy holy one (Devarim 33:8). However, he did not mention the incident of the calf. The only sin found in Aharon was the sin found in Moshe, which was the incident of the waters of Merivah, which I will explain in its place. Some say that Yisrael fooled Aharon. Yisrael made a mold of a calf. Aharon was unaware of this and cast the gold into the fire. They offer as proof, I cast it into the fire, and there came out this calf (Devarim 32:24). However, this is incorrect, for if Aharon was a fool whom simpletons could deceive, why would Elokim have chosen him? Furthermore, why did Aharon build an altar before the calf and command that Yisrael slaughter sacrifices and burnt offerings upon it? Others say that the individual named Aharon who made the calf was not Aharon the brother of Moshe. This too is nonsense, for the congregation that gathered, only gathered against the one who stood in place of Moshe. Scripture clearly states, behold, Aharon and Chur are with you (Shemot 24:14). If the one who made the calf was someone else named Aharon, why didn’t Aharon kill him? Why didn’t Moshe kill him when he came down from the mountain? Moshe even prayed on his behalf. It is not fitting for a pious man to make an idol for others so that they do not die. There are also many who say that the meaning of Tomorrow shall be a feast to Hashem (Shemot 32:5) is that those who served the calf would be killed by Moshe. But the meaning of Tomorrow shall be a feast (chag) to Hashem can only mean that after Aharon built the altar before the calf, he commanded that an announcement be made in the camp that they should slaughter sacrifices the next day on the altar which he built. The meaning of chag (feast) is a sacrifice, as in bind the offering with thick ropes (Tehillim 118:27). This is what Yisrael did, for we read, and they arose early on the morrow, and offered burnt-offerings (Shemot 31:6). Thoughts are of no avail, for one who curses Elokim is killed for what he said. The case is the same with a person who says, Let us go and serve other gods (Devarim 13:7). The one who explains I am Esav thy first-born (Bereshit 27:19) as meaning, I am what I am, but Esav is your first-born, is not offering the plain meaning of the text. Neither is he explaining the text in accordance with the rules of rhetoric. If a person asks his neighbor in a law court, “Are you the one to whom I lent the following sum of money?” and his neighbor responds, “I am,” he cannot later say, “What I meant was, I am his neighbor.” The same also applies to what Daniel said to Nevuchadnetzar: My lord, the dream be to them that hate thee (Daniel 4:16). Daniel spoke according to the rules of etiquette. I will now cite for you the opinion of the Gaon. Rabbi Saadiah said that Aharon, like Yehu, acted with guile. Hence Aharon built the altar. Saadiah Gaon raised the following question against his own interpretation: “If Aharon acted with guile, then why was Elokim angry with him?” The Gaon answered that Elokim was angry with Aharon because he did not immediately kill those who worshipped the calf, as Moshe did when he arrived. However, this too is incorrect, for Aharon called out, Tomorrow shall be a feast to Hashem (YHVH) (32:5). Aharon employed the name YHVH. This name is a proper noun in honor of Hashem. It is not used for any other being. It is not like the name Elokim (Elokim), which is used in many different ways. Furthermore, why didn’t Aharon mention this when he responded to Moshe? For Aharon said, I cast it into the fire (Shemot 32:24). Aharon’s answer is not in keeping with the question. I will now begin to briefly explain part of the secret. Far be it, far be it for Aharon to make an idol. Yisrael also did not ask for an idol. What happened was that Yisrael thought that Moshe, who, as I have explained, had led them on their journey from the Red Sea, had died, for Yisrael noticed that the manna did not come down at Mount Sinai. Furthermore, Moshe tarried on the mountain for forty days. A human being does not have the stamina to live that long without food. Also, Moshe did not tell them when he would descend. Moshe himself did not know this, for Elokim told him, “Come up to Me onto the mount and be there until I give you the tablets of stone.” The word elohim (god) refers to a glorious being dwelling in an image of a body. Yisrael said as follows: who shall go before us (Shemot 32:l). If you pay attention to Yisrael’s first journey you will understand this. The calf was thus made for the glory of Elokim. Hence Aharon built an altar before the calf and announced that they should offer sacrifices on the morrow for the glory of Elokim. Yisrael did as Aharon commanded them. Aharon’s answer was that the people gathered themselves upon him (Shemot 32:l). I have already noted that whenever the verb kahal (gathered) is followed by the word al (upon) it has a negative connotation. However, if it is followed by the word el (to), as in And all the men of Yisrael assembled themselves (va-yikkhal) unto (el) king Shlomo (Melachim I 8:2), then it has a positive connotation. This is the meaning of thou knowest the people, that they are set on evil (Shemot 32:22). The meaning of the verse is: I did not do evil to them. For they merely asked for a being that would go before them. I made the calf for the glory of Elokim. However, [the calf became an object of worship] because there was a mixed multitude among Yisrael. This what Aharon meant by ve-ra hu (they are set on evil). Aharon did not say ra hu (they are evil). A small group of Bnei Yisrael thought that the calf was an idol. They brought sacrifices and bowed to the calf and said, This is thy god, O Yisrael (Shemot 32:4). Do not be amazed that Scripture states, for thy people…have dealt corruptly; they have turned aside quickly out of the way which I commanded them (Shemot 32:7,8), for Scripture does not say all thy people. Can you not see that Achan alone violated the ban and yet Scripture states, Yisrael hath sinned; yea, they have even transgressed My covenant…and have also stolen, and dissembled also, and they have even put it among their own stuff (Yehoshua 7:11). Now, only three thousand Bnei Yisrael, which comes to a half of a tenth of a tenth of the Yisraeli camp, worshipped the golden calf as a god, that is, said, This is thy god, O Yisrael (Shemot 32:4), or thought so in their hearts. The sum of the matter is that we would not be acting properly if we maintain that the calf was made to serve as an idol as the simple-minded believe. Do not be surprised that Elokim was furious with Aharon, because he was the cause of their sin. For look, Aharon was punished along with his brother Moshe concerning the incident at the waters of Merivah. However, Moshe and Aharon did not deliberately sin. Nevertheless, Scripture states regarding them, Because ye believed not in Me (Bamidbar 20:12); ye rebelled (Bamidbar 27:14), and ye trespassed against Me (Devarim 33:51). The astrologers say that the great conjunction of the two upper bodies was in the constellation of Taurus. This is a lie. The conjunction took place in Aquarius. According to the science of astrology this is Yisrael’s constellation. Many have tested this secret, generation after generation. I too have seen this to be the case. Look! They placed it at the midpoint of the sky.

And Aharon said unto them: break off the golden rings. Pareku (break off) is vocalized like barekhu (bless). It is a pi’el. It was the custom of the Mitzrim to place rings in their ears. It is similarly written with regard to the Midyanim, because they were Yishmeelim (Jud. 8:24).
And all the people broke off the golden rings which were in their ears. In the ears of the above-mentioned sons, daughters, and wives.

And he received it at their hand, and fashioned it with a graving tool. The word va-yatzar (and fashioned it) is related to the word tzurah (form). It is like the word va-yatzar (fashioned) in Thus he fashioned the two pillars of brass (Melachim I 7:15).

[With a graving tool.] The word cheret (graving tool) means an image. Be-cheret enosh (in common script) (Is. 8:1) similarly means in the form of a person. There is no reason to connect cheret to the word ha-charitim (the veils) (Is. 3:22).
A molten calf. The word masekhah means molten. It is similar to the word nasakh (hath melted) in The image perchance, which the craftsman hath melted (Is. 40:19).
And when Aharon saw this. In his heart. The word saw here is similar to the word saw in Then I saw (Kohelet 2:13), and the word saw in Now Yaakov saw that there was corn in Mitzrayim (Bereshit 42:1).
And they rose up early on the morrow. Following the day that the altar was built.

And Hashem said. Stiffnecked means that they refuse to do as Elokim commanded. They are like a person who runs along on his way and does not turn his head back to the one who calls him. This expression is employed with regard to Bnei Yisrael for the following reason. Scripture tells us that Yisrael served idols in Mitzrayim. It reports that Elokim sent prophets to them saying, “Let every man cast away the idols of Mitzrayim.” Moshe related this incident to their children before he died. Moshe employed different terminology. However, the import of the words is the same as here. Scripture here states that Elokim told Moshe, Go, get thee down; for thy people…have dealt corruptly (v. 7). However, Moshe later quoted Elokim as saying, Arise, get thee down (Devarim 19:12). Scripture there writes, This is thy god, O Yisrael (v. 8). Scripture goes on to say here, Now therefore let Me alone (ve-attah ha-nichah li) (v. 10). However, it later reads, let Me alone (heref mi-menni) (Devarim 9:14). Scripture here reads, that My wrath may wax hot against them, and that I may consume them (v. 10). However, it later reads, that I may destroy them and blot out their name (Devarim 9:14). Scripture here reads, and I will make of thee a great nation (v. 10). However, Moshe later quoted Elokim as saying, and I will make of thee a nation mightier [and greater than they] (Devarim 9:14). The meanings are the same.

Now therefore let me alone, that my wrath may wax hot against them, and that I may consume them.] God hinted to Moshe that were He not concerned with Moshe’s glory, He would destroy Yisrael. Hence Moshe was compelled to pray.

And Moshe besought. We encounter verbs from the root chet, lamed, heh that have this meaning only with regard to the face. Compare, Many will entreat (yechallu) the favour of the liberal man (Mishlei 19:6). I believe that it is similar to and her face was no more (Shmuel I 1:18). They are all similar. It is therefore incorrect to say chillitikha or achallekha, for chillitikha and achallekha are related to the word chillah (sick) in wherewith Hashem hath made it sick (Devarim 29:21). Some commentaries say that this prayer is the same prayer found in the Torah portion Ve-Hayah Ekev. This prayer should have been recorded following Moshe’s return to the mountain (v. 31). Therefore Hashem repented of the evil (v. 14) after Moshe prayed and fell upon his face for forty days (Devarim 10:10). If Hashem repented first, what reason was there for Moshe to say, peradventure I shall make atonement for your sin (v. 30)? The sequence of events was as follows: Moshe descended, burned the calf, and killed its worshippers. He then returned to pray to Hashem on behalf of Yisrael and on behalf of Aharon, who was the cause. Others say that the prayer O Hashem Hashem, destroy not Thy people (Devarim 9:26) is not the prayer which is mentioned here. I believe that the contents of both prayers are the same. I will later explain this point. For how could Moshe beg Hashem [not to destroy Yisrael] before he burned the calf, caused Yisrael to drink, and killed its worshippers? Hashem only hinted to Moshe that he should pray after he descended and removed the calf. Hence after Moshe removed their sin Scripture reads, peradventure I shall make atonement for your sin (v. 30). We similarly read, And I took your sin, the calf which ye had made, [and burnt it with fire] (Devarim 9:21). It was only because Hashem told Moshe, Now therefore let Me alone, that My wrath may wax hot against them (v. 10) that Moshe mentioned the prayer that he prayed when he fell down before Hashem. Actually, this chapter should have been written after And Moshe returned unto Hashem (v. 31). However, there is no chronological order in the Torah. Scripture was only concerned with connecting the statement Whosoever hath sinned against Me, [him will I blot out] (v. 33) with And now go, lead the people (v. 34). Scripture goes on to state, And Hashem smote the people (v. 35).

Besought. Look. Scripture writes, So I fell down before Hashem the forty days and forty nights that I fell down; because Hashem had said he would destroy you (Devarim 9:25). This is what let Me alone, that I may destroy them (Devarim 9:14) refers to. The mind cannot accept the idea that Moshe prayed on behalf of Yisrael while an idol was among them. He first removed the idol.

Now, Hashem, why doth Thy wrath wax hot against Thy people is similar to O Hashem Hashem, destroy not Thy people and Thine inheritance (Devarim 9:26). Scripture then goes on to say, that Thou didst bring out by Thy great power and by Thy outstretched arm (Devarim 9:29). This is parallel to that Thou hast brought forth out of the land of Mitzrayim with great power and with a mighty hand. Scripture writes, Remember Thy servants, Avraham, Yitzchak, and Yaakov (Devarim 9:27). This is parallel to Remember Avraham, Yitzchak, and Yisrael, Thy servants, to whom Thou didst swear by Thine own self (v. 13). Its meaning is, remember the oath which you swore to them. Scripture does not mention the oath in the verse that reads, Remember Thy servants (Devarim 9:27). For there is a difference in meaning between zekhor la’avadekha (remember Thy servants) (Devarim 9:27) and zekhor adatekha (remember Thy congregation) in Remember Thy congregation, which Thou hast gotten of old (Tehillim 74:2), because of the lamed. Now, lest the land whence Thou broughtest us out say (Devarim 9:28) is parallel to Wherefore should the Mitzrim speak, saying (v. 12).

[For evil did he bring them forth.] The meaning of be-ra’a hotzi’am (for evil did He bring them forth) is, as our ancients hint, that they went out of Mitzrayim under a star called ra (evil). Now Mitzrayim will say that Hashem does not have the ability to overcome the power of this star and save those who cleave to him. Hence when He saw that He was unable to overcome the star, He killed them. This will desecrate Hashem’s name. Now Moshe fell before Hashem forty days. Hashem then told him, for I will not go up in the midst of thee (Shemot 33:3). They will thus not inherit the land. Moshe then said everything contained in the portion that opens with the words, See, Thou sayest unto me (Shemot 33:12). Hashem then commanded him to descend, hew out tablets, and carry them in his hands up to the mountain. Hashem then descended in a cloud and the skin of Moshe’s face sent forth beams. Hashem then wrote the second tablets. Scripture therefore reads, At that time Hashem said unto me: Hew thee two tables of stone like unto the first…and make thee an ark of wood (Devarim 10:1). Yisrael was thus told to make the ark. This is the ark that Betzalel made.

And Hashem repented. Heaven forbid for Hashem to repent. Rather, Scripture employed human terminology. Compare, And Hashem went up (Bereshit 35:13); And Hashem came down (Bereshit 11:5); Let Hashem rejoice in His works (Tehillim 105:31), and, And it grieved Him at His heart (Bereshit 6:6). Look, Shmuel said, And also the Glory of Yisrael will not lie nor repent (Shmuel I 15:29). Nevertheless, Scripture there reads, It repenteth Me (Shmuel I 15:11). There are those who explain va-yinachem (repented) by the Arabic word wa’ad. However, there is no need for this.

And Moshe turned. Scripture here tells us, and the mount burned with fire (Devarim 9:15). The meaning of and Moshe turned is that Moshe looked around like a person who looks around and contemplates his course of action. Moshe saw that he had to descend quickly. Va-yifen (turned) here is similar to va-yifen koh va-kho (and he looked this way and that way) (Shemot 2:12).

[In his hand.] In his possession. It is similar to And take with thee ten men. For we cannot understand how Moshe was able to bring down one tablet in his hand. It is next to impossible to believe that he carried down two tablets in his hand.

[Tables that were written on both their sides.] Now since Scripture explicitly tells us that the tablets were written on both sides, they could not have been made out of any of the stones that are mentioned with regard to the breastplate, for what was seen on one side would then be seen on the other side. The word ketuvim (written) does not mean seen. Ketuvim means written. Scripture tells us that what was written on one side was also written on the other side. Each tablet was thus thick. There is no need to assume that the mem and the samekh which were inscribed in the tablets were miraculously suspended, for there is a difference of opinion regarding the meaning of the term ashurit. Some believe that the word ashurit means a praise-worthy script. Others maintain that it refers to the script which they brought up from Ashur. Furthermore, if the letters were visible on the reverse side, then the letters would appear backwards. There is no room for one to argue with me and ask whether these stones were precious. The answer is that the stones were very precious because the writing of Elokim was engraved upon them. The stones had to be thick. Where would Moshe find very precious stones that were a cubit in length, a cubit and a half in width, and a cubit in height? Furthermore, where would Moshe get the raw material to hew out two tablets of precious stones of the same dimensions as the first stones? Now we do not know the way the Ten Statements were written on the two tablets without Moshe having to turn them over. Hence after telling us that were written on both their sides, Scripture goes on to say, on the one side and on the other side were they written. We have no way of knowing whether each one of the tablets was completely covered with writing, or whether some blank spaces were left on the four corners as we do today with our books. We similarly do not know whether the writing was thick or thin. There is no reason for us to speculate concerning things for which we do not have a tradition.

And the tables were the work of Elokim. Our ancients said that it was decreed that they be like this. I have already explained this at the beginning of the Book of Bereshit. However, I believe that the meaning of the work of Elokim is that they were created in their proper dimensions. This is mentioned because of the second tablets, which Moshe hewed out.

[Graven.] Some say that the word charut means charush (graven). Others invert the letters and come up with the word chatar (dig) (Yechezkel 8:8). Actually, the word has no counterpart [is a hapax legomenon]. It is possibly similar in meaning to the word patu’ach (engraved).
And when Yehoshua heard. And when Yehoshua, who remained at the foot of the mountain, heard.

As they shouted. The word be-re’o (as they shouted) is related to the word tru’ah (shouting). As the word de’iy (my knowledge) in I will fetch my knowledge from afar (Iyov. 36:3) is derived from yada, so is the word yara derived from re’o. The same applies to lamah tri’iy re’a (why dost thou cry out aloud) (Michah 4:9).

And he said. Saadiah Gaon says that Yehoshua also said this. However, I believe that these are the words of Moshe. And it came to pass, as soon as he came nigh unto the camp which follows (v. 19) is proof of this.
Being overcome. The word chalushah (overcome) is a noun. It is similar to the word gevurah (mastery).
The noise of them that sing. Anot (that sing) means tunes. This is what and rose up to make merry refers to (v. 6).

That he saw the calf and the dancing. The heh prefixed to the word egel (calf) also refers to the word u-mecholot (and the dancing). The verse should be understood as follows: that he saw the calf and the dancing around it. Moshe was overcome by great jealousy. He therefore broke the tablets which were in his hands and served, as it were, as a document of witness Moshe thus tore up the contract. As Scripture states, he did this in the sight of all of Yisrael.

And he took the calf. Some say that the meaning of and burnt it with fire is that he melted it in fire. However, there is no need for this, for there is a substance which, when put into the fire along with the gold, causes the gold to immediately catch fire, turn black, and never again turn back into gold. This has been tested and found to be true.

And strewed it upon the water. The reference is to the water from the brook that descended out of the mountain. Moshe commanded all of Yisrael to drink from these waters. This was similar to and of the dust that is on the floor of the tabernacle the priest shall take, and put it into the water (Bamidbar 5:17). Now the water caused a sign to appear on the face of those who served the calf or their bellies swelled up. For otherwise, how could the Leviyim know who worshipped the golden calf? We have already said that very few of Bnei Yisrael had evil thoughts. The intention of all was to do good.
And Moshe said. Observe. Moshe asked why Aharon needed to make the calf.
And Aharon said: let not the anger of my Lord wax hot. Aharon called Moshe my lord because of Moshe’s great station.
[That they are set on evil.] I have already explained the meaning of that they are set on evil. Similarly, So they said unto me (v. 23) and, And I said unto them (v. 24).

And when Moshe saw that the people were broken loose. The word paru’a (broken loose) is similar to yippare’a (cast off restraint) in Where there is no vision, the people cast off restraint (Mishlei 28:18), and va-tifre’u (ye have set at nought) in But ye have set at nought all my counsel (Mishlei 1:25).
[For a derision.] Scripture employs an adjective (le-shimtzah) in place of an infinitive. The meaning of le-shimtzah (for a derision) is that they will be a derision, a blemish, a defamation.

Among their enemies. Kamehem (their enemies) is similar to kamim alai (rise up against me) in Many are they that rise up against me (Tehillim 3:2) and the abridged form kamai (rise up against me) in that rise up against me (Tehillim 18:49). However, the Aramaic translation connects kamehem to the word kamtem (ye are risen) in And, behold, ye are risen up in your fathers’ stead (Bamidbar 32:14).

Then Moshe stood. It is the practice of all camps that stay in one place for about a year to erect booths and have gates. In such a case, there is no need to set aside a place outside the camp as a latrine.
Whoso is on Hashem’s side. Shall draw close to me; shall come near to me; shall come to me or shall gather to me.
The sons of Levi. Who were of Moshe’s family.
And he said unto them. Moshe referred to the Lord as the Elokim of Yisrael because those who worshipped the calf thought that the Lord was to be identified with the calf.

And slay every man his brother. Even if it be his brother. Many interpret Who said of his father, and of his mother: I have not seen him (Devarim 33:9) as referring to this incident. They had to explain his father and his mother as referring to the father of the mother. However, as I will explain, there is no need for this interpretation.
And the sons of Levi did. Not all the sons of Levi.
And Moshe said. Its meaning is, and Moshe already said to them. It is similar to Then Hashem Elokim formed (Bereshit 2:7). There are many other such examples.
[Consecrate.] The word milu (consecrate), which is in the kal, is grammatically irregular. It is sometimes transitive and at other times intransitive.

[For every man hath been against his son.] Even if the worshipper be his son or brother he must kill him. They will be rewarded with a blessing for doing this. This is what At that time Hashem separated the tribe of Levi (Devarim 10:8) refers to. Its meaning is that Hashem told Moshe at Mount Sinai the reason the tribe of Levi was set aside. Scripture therefore reads, Now these are the generations of Aharon and Moshe in the day that Hashem spoke with Moshe in mount Sinai (Bamidbar 3:1). Now Aharon, his sons, and the Leviyim were separated to serve Hashem at the time that the tabernacle was erected. Korach’s quarrel took place at that time. Korach was a first-born. Korach rebelled when Hashem set aside the Leviyim in place of the first-born who were holy. Hashem did this because the first-born brought the burnt offerings before the calf and they slaughtered peace offerings upon the altar, which was made before the calf.
And it came to pass on the morrow. Following his descent.

And now I will go up. To return to the mountain to fall before Hashem and atone for Yisrael as I have explained. Perhaps Hashem will write another pair of tablets in order to make a covenant with Yisrael. This is the meaning of Behold, I make a covenant (Shemot 34:10). For the tablets were, as it were, a document of witness.

And Moshe returned. The Nagid says that a lamed has been dropped and compensated for in the word anna (oh), which is short for al na (please consent). He maintains that the word al is related to the word ho’il (consent). However, this is far-fetched. On the contrary, its meaning is: please (anna) don’t do this. Anna is an expression of appeasement, or confession, as here. Anna (I beseech Thee) in I beseech Thee, O Hashem, for I am Thy servant (Tehillim 116:16) is similar.

Yet now…blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book. I have already explained in my comments on And the books were opened, in the Book of Daniel (7:10), that all the decrees regarding masses and individuals are contingent upon the arrangements in the sky. Our sages have already admitted that children, longevity, and prosperity [depend upon the influence of the stars]. However, Hashem, as I have explained, increases the good which the heavenly arrangements have decreed because of a person’s fear of Hashem.

And Hashem said. Saadiah Gaon says that this is what And Hashem repented (v. 14) refers to, for Hashem had said that He would destroy all. The meaning of our verse is: Look. I will blot out of My book only those who sinned against Me in their minds. The aforementioned is to be understood after the manner of that I may take the house of Yisrael in their own heart (Yechezkel 14:5). They were not killed because they did not actually worship the calf. This is the meaning of: And Hashem smote the people, because the calf was made and doubt came to people privately.

And now go, lead the people unto the place of which I have spoken unto thee. That is, unto the place of the Kenaani (Shemot 3:8). This was said in anger. God told Moshe, I have forgiven their sin because of you. Now you, who love them so much, go lead them.
In the day. The beginning of every year is the day of accounting.
And the Lord smote. It is possible that there was no plague in the first year. The Torah merely reports what happened after they journeyed from Mount Sinai.

And the Lord spoke unto Moshe: depart, go up hence. Scripture reads go up because one who goes towards the left side goes up. Avraham therefore went down into Mitzrayim (Bereshit 12:10) because he was in the south.
[Yaakov.] I will do all of this because of the oath which I swore to Avraham, Yitzchak, and Yaakov.
And I will send an angel before thee. To help you.
[An angel.] Scripture does not read the angel because the angel refers to the angel which is known to have Hashem’s name in him.
For I will not go up in the midst of thee. They will not erect the tabernacle, for I will not rest in the midst of Yisrael.

[Lest I consume thee in the way.] I will immediately consume them if they once again act in this manner. Akhelkha (I consume thee) is vocalized with a segol in place of a pattach, and its lamed does not have a dagesh in it even though the rules of grammar require it. Compare the word achavvekha (I will tell thee) in I will tell thee, hear thou me (Iyov 15:17).

And when the people heard these evil tidings. What evil tidings? The reference is to what is written afterwards, And Hashem said unto Moshe, etc. (v. 5). And Hashem said unto Moshe (Shemot 4:19) is similar. I have already explained the meaning of Can He give bread also (Tehillim 78:20). It is like And He commanded the skies above (Tehillim 78:23), the meaning of which is, and He had already commanded the skies. This is also the case here. There is no need for the Geonic interpretation to the effect that they always did so.

And the children of Yisrael stripped themselves of their ornaments. Et edyam means of their ornaments. The reference is to their fine garments and ornaments such as rings worn on the ears and fingers. The word edyam is to be interpreted in light of va-edekh edi (I decked thee also with ornaments) (Yechezkel 16:11). Yisrael stripped themselves of their ornaments because they mourned over the incident of the calf.
Now Moshe used to take the tent. Scripture employs an imperfect in place of a perfect. We find the same in They made a calf in Chorev (Tehillim 106:19).
The tent. His tent. It is like and they came into the tent (Shemot 18:7).

[Now Moshe used to take the tent and pitch it without the camp, afar off from the camp; and he called it the Tent of Meeting.] Look. Moshe was separated from Yisrael because of the Glory that used to speak with him. This took place after he brought down the inscribed second tablets and Yisrael began to construct the tabernacle. Moshe called his tent the tent of meeting because Hashem met with him there until the tabernacle was erected. There is no chronological order in the Torah. Some say that the tent refers to the tabernacle and that Scripture tells us where the tabernacle was located during the fifty days before the banners were set up.
And it came to pass. This too was a sign. Yisrael saw that as soon as Moshe came to the tent from the camp of Bnei Yisrael he immediately saw the pillar of cloud.

And when all the people saw. This took place after what is reported in the section beginning with the words, See, Thou sayest unto me (v. 12), for what is recorded in the latter chapter occurred during the forty days that Moshe fell before Hashem concerning the incident of the calf. After this, Moshe descended and hewed out the stones. Hashem then passed by Moshe, and this led to the fulfillment of Hashem’s word, and thou shalt see My back (v. 23).
And Hashem spoke unto Moshe face to face. I will explain this in a section that will soon follow.

But his minister Yehoshua, the son of nun, a young man. Yehoshua lived a hundred and ten years. Our sages said that Yehoshua spent seven years conquering Kenaan and seven years dividing it up. If this is the case, then Yehoshua was now fifty-six years old. Why then did Scripture call him a young man? This is its grammatical explanation. His minister Yehoshua, the son of Nun, performed the service of a young man.
And Moshe said unto the Lord: see, thou sayest unto me. See means see the predicament in which I find myself. I will now grammatically explain the section.
[I know thee.] Rabbi Saadiah Gaon says that yedatikha (I know thee) means I have honored thee. However, this is incorrect, for that I may know Thee (v. 13) just as You know me follows.

[My presence.] Saadiah Gaon says that the meaning of the word panai (my presence) means my anger, as in u-fanehah lo hayu lah od (and her countenance was no more sad) (Shmuel I 1:18). Now, what will the Gaon do with the word panekha (thy presence) in If Thy presence go not with me (v. 15)? I believe that panai means I, myself. It is similar to the word panekha (thine own person) in and that thou go to battle in thine own person (panekha) (Shmuel II 17:11).

So that we are distinguished. Ve-niflinu (so that we are distinguished) comes from the same root as ve-hiflah (shall make a division) in And Hashem shall make a division (Shemot 9:4). It belongs to those roots which end in a heh.

Thy glory. Your very self, for Scripture explicitly states, And it shall come to pass, while My glory passeth by, that I will put thee in a cleft of the rock, and will cover thee with My hand until I have passed by (v. 22).

And will proclaim the name of Hashem. Scripture writes with regard to Avraham, and (he) called upon the name (be-shem) of Hashem (Bereshit 12:8). People were the ones who were called upon to serve Hashem. The word be-shem (upon the name) is therefore connected to Hashem’s glorious name. However, this is not the case with and proclaimed the name of Hashem (Shemot 34:5), for here Hashem is the one who calls. It is the same case with and will proclaim the name of Hashem before thee.

See me. The word yirani (see me) is vocalized with a kamatz. It is vocalized like ro’ani (seeth me) in And sayest none seeth me (Is. 47:10), and le-hotzi’anu (to bring us forth) in to bring us forth out of Mitzrayim (Shemot 14:11), and yeshivani (bring me back) in If Hashem shall indeed bring me back to Yerushalayim (Shmuel II 15:8).

[And live.] The meaning of va-chai (and live) is, and will live. [FOR MAN SHALL NOT SEE ME AND LIVE.] For he will immediately die. Thus, upon seeing Elokim’s messenger, Manoach said, We shall surely die, because we have seen an angel (Jud. 13:22).
